punchline: Nobody remembers King's 'I Have a Plan' speech, because he never gave one.
thirty_sec: In the summer of 1963, about 250,000 people gathered in Washington to hear Martin Luther King Jr. There were no invitations and no website, yet they came. Simon Sinek argues they didn't come for King himself. They came because he voiced a belief they already held. He gave the 'I Have a Dream' speech, not an 'I Have a Plan' speech, and people who shared the dream made his cause their own.
question: If you lost your slides before your next big pitch, what would you still believe strongly enough to say?
